purpose: Market Microstructure Analytics estimates spread and liquidity stress from ordinary chart bars, helping users compare execution conditions with their own recent history. Its outputs are statistical proxies for transaction mechanics rather than observations of the exchange order book.
mechanism: Roll spread uses twice the square root of negative lagged price-change covariance. Corwin–Schultz separates single- and paired-bar high/low ranges; Abdi–Ranaldo uses the close displacement from the log high/low midpoint and adjacent displacement products, excluding invalid flat-range pairs. A separate effective-spread proxy combines tick-rule direction and displacement from the bar midpoint.

Amihud divides absolute log return by dollar volume. Kyle lambda regresses absolute price changes on unnormalized signed bar volume; Parkinson range volatility supplies a spread/volatility comparison. Smoothed spread estimates receive inverse robust-variance weights with ridge stabilization and a weight cap.
Spread, illiquidity and absolute-lambda robust z-scores are individually clipped and averaged, then transformed with tanh into the Liquidity Stress Index.
outputs_and_use: Dashboard estimates, weights, stress/regime readings and the spread trend help assess whether trading conditions are becoming unusually expensive. A fast-versus-slow composite-spread EMA comparison indicates widening or compression without specifying price direction.
parameters: Estimation window defaults to 20 bars; smoothing 1 disables EMA smoothing. Maximum composite weight defaults to 70%, with a ridge equal to 5% of mean robust variance. LSI clipping defaults to three robust deviations. Spread-trend EMAs use five and twenty periods.
risks: Aggregated-bar covariance and tick-rule direction differ from transaction-level observations. The midpoint effective-spread proxy is upward biased, while Roll aggregation can understate spread. Elevated lambda alone does not prove informed trading; historical crisis narratives are not measured predictive results.

purpose: Markov Chain [3D] summarizes recent transitions among detected bullish, bearish and neutral regimes. Its animated state diagram is paired with a numeric bias output intended for connecting regime filters to separately specified systematic trading rules.
mechanism: The engine standardizes price returns or three equally weighted custom series with rolling Z-scores, classifies normalized values into market states and smooths combined custom classifications. purpose: DEAM recommends a changing US-equity versus cash allocation by combining market regime, risk capacity, valuation, sentiment and macro conditions. It is a tactical exposure model with a separate crisis override, not a documented executed portfolio or verified return record.
mechanism: Trend relationships, annualized volatility and drawdown form the regime score. Risk allocation compares target volatility with the larger close-return/Parkinson estimate and target drawdown with market drawdown; an exponential penalty reduces overutilized risk.

Valuation blends earnings yield, buybacks, dividend-growth and shareholder-yield approaches to equity risk premium, then applies profitability, growth and leverage adjustments. Sentiment uses VIX normalization, term structure and safe-haven relative performance; macro scores use Treasury spreads, bond credit proxies and balance-sheet quality.

Weighted component allocations receive a model-style adjustment and moving-average smoothing. A stress counter combines volatility, drawdown, credit, simultaneous stock/bond losses and panic volume; crisis states cap exposure.
outputs_and_use: Allocation and complementary cash series, component scores, regime/crisis dashboard and threshold alerts support portfolio reviews. Optional allocation-dispersion bands describe recent recommendation variability, not calibrated confidence in future returns. Users must choose a rebalancing and execution policy.
parameters: Default target annual volatility is 12% and maximum drawdown 15%. Default component weights are regime/risk/valuation/sentiment/macro 35/25/20/15/5 percent; final smoothing uses three periods. Crisis and severe-crisis exposure caps are 25% and 10%.
